questions.question: If 21 tan θ = 20, then(1 + sin θ - cos θ) : (1 - sin θ + cos θ) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If 21 tan θ = 20, then(1 + sin θ - cos θ) : (1 - sin θ + cos θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

21 tan θ = 20

Concept used:

tanθ = P/B

sinθ = P/H

cosθ = B/H

P = perpendicular

B = base

H= hypotenuse

Calculation:

We know 20, 21 and, 29 is a Pythagorean triplets

So, 21 tan θ = 20

⇒ tanθ = 20/21

⇒ sinθ = 20/29

⇒ cosθ = 21/29

(1 + sin θ - cos θ) : (1 - sin θ + cos θ)

⇒ (1 + 20/29 - 21/29) : (1 - 20/29 + 21/29)

⇒ (29 + 20 - 21)/29 : (29 - 20 + 21)/29

⇒ 28 : 30

⇒ 14 : 15

∴ Required value is 14 : 15

questions.question: \(\frac{{\sqrt {\ cosec x - 1} }}{{\sqrt {\ cosec x + 1} }}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: \(\frac{{\sqrt {\ cosec x - 1} }}{{\sqrt {\ cosec x + 1} }}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

√(cosecx – 1)/√(cosecx + 1)  

Trigonometry identities used:

sin2x + cos2x = 1

Formula used:

 a2 – b2 = (a + b) (a – b)

Calculation:

⇒ √(cosecx – 1)/√(cosecx + 1) 

(Here cosecx = 1/sinx

⇒ √[(1/sinx) – 1]/√[(1/sinx) + 1]

⇒ √(1 – sinx)/√(1 + sinx)

Rationalization

⇒ [√(1 – sinx)/√(1 + sinx)] ×  [√(1 – sinx)/√(1 – sinx)]   

⇒ √(1 – sinx)2/√(1 + sinx) (1 – sinx)

Here a2 – b2 = (a + b) (a – b)

⇒ (1 – sinx)/√(1 – sin2x)

Here 1 – sin2x = cos2x

⇒ (1 – sinx)/√cos2x

⇒ (1 – sinx)/cosx

⇒ (1/cosx) – (sinx/cosx)

Here 1/cosx = secx, sinx/cosx = tanx

⇒ secx – tanx    

∴ The required answer is secx - tanx

questions.question: If 3cos 2 θ - 4sinθ + 1 = 0 , 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of 3cos 2 θ + 5tan 2 θ will be:
questions.questionHtml: If 3cos2θ - 4sinθ + 1 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of 3cos2θ + 5tan2θ will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

3cos2θ - 4sinθ + 1

Formula used:

b2 = h2 – p2

Cos2θ = 1 – sin2θ 

Calculation:

3cos2θ - 4sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 3 (1 – sin2θ – 4 sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 3 – 3sin2θ – 4sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 3sin2θ + 4sinθ – 4 = 0

⇒ 3sin2θ + 6sinθ – 2sinθ – 4 = 0

⇒ 3sinθ (sinθ + 2) – 2(sinθ + 2) = 0

⇒ sinθ = 2/3, -2

Now,

sinθ = p/h = 2/3

b2 = h2 – p2

⇒ b2 = (9 – 4)

⇒ b2= 5

⇒ b = √5

cosθ = b/h = √5/3

tanθ = p/b = 2/√5

3cos2θ + 5tan2θ = (3 × 5/9) + (5 × 4/5)

⇒ (5/3 + 4)

⇒ 17/3

⇒ \(5\frac{2}{3}\)

∴ The required value is \(5\frac{2}{3}\)

Calculation 

⇒ cos A/(cosec A + 1) + cosA/(cosecA - 1) = 2 

⇒ [cos A(cosec A - 1) + cos A(cosec A + 1)]/[cosec2 A - 1] = 2 

⇒ (2 cos A cosec A)/cot2 A = 2

⇒ cos A cosec A/(cos2/sin A) = 1 [ cot A = cos A/sin A] 

⇒ tan A = 1 

⇒ tan A = tan 45° 

⇒ A = 45°

questions.question: If 6 cos 2 θ + cos θ = 2, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of (cosec θ + cot θ + tan θ) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 6 cos<sup>2 </sup>θ + cos θ = 2, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of (cosec θ + cot θ + tan θ) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

6 cos2 θ + cos θ = 2

Concept used:

Solve the quadratic equation by factorization method.

Calculation:

6 cos2 θ + cos θ = 2

⇒ 6 cos2 θ + cos θ - 2 = 0

⇒ 6 cos2 θ + 4cos θ - 3cos θ - 2 = 0

⇒ 2cos θ (3cos θ + 2) -1(3cos θ + 2) = 0 

⇒ (3cos θ + 2)(2cos θ - 1) = 0

Now, we have-

3cos θ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos θ = -2/3

But, as we know that the value of cosine function is positive in the interval 0° < θ < 90°, this value will be rejected.

Now,

2cos θ = 1

⇒ cos θ = 1/2

⇒ θ = 60° 

Now,

cosec θ + cot θ + tan θ

⇒ cosec 60° + cot 60° + tan 60°

⇒ 2/√3 + 1/√3 + √3

⇒ 3/√3 + √3

⇒ 2√3

∴ The value of (cosec θ + cot θ + tan θ) is 2√3.

questions.question: If tan θ + cot θ = 3, then what will be the value of tan 2 θ + cot 2 θ ?
questions.questionHtml: If tan θ + cot θ = 3, then what will be the value of tan<sup>2</sup> θ + cot<sup>2</sup> θ ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any expression of the form x + (1/x) = k, the value of x2 + (1/x2) is always k2 − 2.

Since cot θ = 1/tan θ, we have tan θ + (1/tan θ) = 3.

Value = 32 − 2 = 9 − 2 = 7.

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Alternate Method

Given: tan θ + cot θ = 3

Formula Used: (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

⇒ (tan θ + cot θ)2 = 32

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2(tan θ)(cot θ) = 9

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2(1) = 9

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ = 9 − 2

⇒ tan2 θ + cot2 θ = 7

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric pairs that are reciprocals: tan θ × cot θ = 1, sin θ × cosec θ = 1, and cos θ × sec θ = 1.

Higher Powers Shortcut

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k and x4 + 1/x4 = (k2 − 2)2 − 2.

Pythagorean Identities

Key formulas include sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1 and cosec2 θ − cot2 θ = 1.

questions.question: If 7 cos 2 θ + 5 sin 2 θ - 6 = 0, (0° < θ < 90°), then what is the value of \(\sqrt {\frac{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ +\ \cot θ }}{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ -\ \cot θ }}} \) ?
questions.questionHtml: If 7 cos2 θ + 5 sin2 θ - 6 = 0, (0° < θ < 90°), then what is the value of \(\sqrt {\frac{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ +\ \cot θ }}{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ -\ \cot θ }}} \) ?
questions.solution:
Given:

7 cos2 θ + 5 sin2 θ - 6 = 0

Concept used:

The value of cosine function is always positive in the interval 0° < θ° < 90°.

Calculation:

7 cos2 θ + 5 sin2 θ - 6 = 0

⇒ 7 cos2 θ + 5 (1 - cos2 θ) - 6 = 0

⇒ 7 cos2 θ + 5 - 5cos2 θ - 6 = 0

⇒ 2 cos2 θ = 1

⇒ cos2 θ = 1/2

⇒ cos θ = 1/√2

⇒ θ = 45° 

Now,

\(√ {\frac{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ +\ \cot θ }}{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ -\ \cot θ }}} \)

⇒ \(√ {\frac{{\text{cosec} \ 45 +\ \cot 45 }}{{\text{cosec} \ 45\ -\ \cot 45 }}} \)

⇒ \(√ {\frac{√2 + 1}{√2 - 1}} \)

⇒ \(√ {\frac{√2 + 1}{√2 - 1} \times \frac{√2 + 1}{√2 + 1}}\)

⇒ √2 + 1

∴ The value of  \(√ {\frac{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ +\ \cot θ }}{{\text{cosec} \ θ\ -\ \cot θ }}} \) is √2 + 1.

questions.question: If 2cos 2 θ = 3 (1 – sinθ), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (tan2θ + cosec3θ – sec2θ) ?
questions.questionHtml: If 2cos2θ = 3 (1 – sinθ), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (tan2θ + cosec3θ – sec2θ) ?
questions.solution:
Given:

2cos2θ = 3 (1 – sinθ)

Formula used:

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

⇒ 1 – sin2θ = cos2θ 

Calculation:

2cos2θ = 3 (1 – sinθ)

⇒ 2cos2θ = 3 – 3sinθ 

⇒ 2cos2θ + 3sinθ – 3 = 0

⇒ 2(1 – sin2θ) + 3sinθ – 3 = 0

⇒ 2 – 2sin2θ + 3sinθ – 3 = 0

⇒ 2sin2θ – 3sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sin2θ – 2sinθ – sinθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sinθ(sinθ – 1) – 1(sinθ – 1) = 0

⇒ (2sinθ – 1) (sinθ – 1) = 0

⇒ sinθ = 1/2 or 1

sinθ = 1/2 = 30°  [sin90° = 1, but 0° < θ < 90° so, we cannot take this value]

⇒ So, θ = 30° 

The value of (tan2θ + cosec3θ – sec2θ) = (tan60° + cosec90° – sec60°)

⇒ (√3 + 1 – 2)

⇒ √3 – 1

∴ The required value is √3 – 1

Shortcut Trick

If we put θ = 30°, it satisfy the equation 2cos2θ = 3 (1 – sinθ)

So,

⇒ (tan2θ + cosec3θ – sec2θ)

⇒ tan 60° + cosec 60° - sec 60° 

⇒ √3 + 1 - 2

⇒ √3 - 1

questions.question: If sin θ( 2 sin θ + 3) = 2, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (sec 2 θ + cot 2 θ - cos 2 θ)?

 sin θ( 2 sin θ + 3) = 2

(sec2 θ + cot2 θ - cos2 θ)

questions.question: If a SinA + b cosA = c, then a cosA - b sinA is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If a SinA + b cosA = c, then a cosA - b sinA is equal to:
questions.solution:
GIven:

a SinA + b cosA = c

Formula used:

If a Sinθ + b Cosθ = c

Then, a Cosθ – b Sinθ = \(√ {{a^2} + {b^2} - {c^2}}\)

Calculation:

Apply above formula on a SinA + b cosA = c 

We get

⇒ a CosA – b SinA = \(√ {{a^2} + {b^2} - {c^2}}\)

∴ a CosA – b SinA is equla to  \(√ {{a^2} + {b^2} - {c^2}}\)

 Alternate Method

Given, a sinA + b cosA = c             -----(1)

Let, x = a cosA - b sinA                  -----(2)

On Square equation (1)

⇒ a2 sin2A + b2cos2A + 2a sinA × b cosA = c2      -----(3)

On Square equation (2)

⇒ a2 cos2A + b2 sin2A - 2a cosA × b sinA = x2      -----(4)

On adding (3) and (4)

⇒ x2 + c2 = a2 + b2

⇒ x = √(a2 + b2 - c2)

∴ a CosA – b SinA is equla to  √(a2 + b2 - c2).

questions.question: If \(2x = \sin \theta \) and \(\frac{2}{x} =\cos \theta \) , then the value of \(4\left( {{x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}} \right)\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(2x = \sin \theta \) and \(\frac{2}{x} =\cos \theta \), then the value of \(4\left( {{x^2} + \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}} \right)\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sinθ = 2x 

cosθ = 2/x

Formula used:

Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 1

Calculation:

⇒ sinθ = 2x 

⇒ sin2θ = 4x2 ---------(1)

⇒ cosθ = 2/x

⇒ cos2θ = 4/x2---------(2)    Add (1) and (2)

⇒ Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 4x2 + 4/x2 

⇒ 4x2 + 4/x2 = 1

⇒ 4(x2 + 1/x2) = 1

questions.question: If \(\frac{\cot \theta + \cos \theta}{\cot \theta - \cos \theta}=\frac{k+1}{1-k}, k \ne 1\) , then k is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{\cot \theta + \cos \theta}{\cot \theta - \cos \theta}=\frac{k+1}{1-k}, k \ne 1\), then k is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{\cot θ + \cos θ}{\cot θ - \cos θ}=\frac{k+1}{1-k}, k \ne 1\)

Formula used:

Componendo and Dividendo

(a + b)/(a – b) = (b + a)/(b – a)

Calculation:

According to the question

\(\frac{\cot θ + \cos θ}{\cot θ - \cos θ}=\frac{k+1}{1-k}, k \ne 1\)

By Componendo and Dividendo

(a + b)/(a – b) = (b + a)/(b – a)

⇒ (cotθ + cosθ)/(cotθ – cosθ) = (cosθ + cotθ)/(cosθ – cotθ) = [(k + 1)/(1 – k) = (1 + k)/(k – 1)

⇒ 2cotθ/2cosθ = 2/2k

⇒ 2cosθ/sinθ/2cosθ = 1/k

⇒ 1/sinθ = 1/k

⇒ k = sinθ 

∴ The required value of k is sinθ

questions.question: If θ = 120° and p = cos θ + sin θ, then :
questions.questionHtml: If θ = 120° and p = cos θ  + sin θ, then :
questions.solution:
p = cos(120°) + sin(120°)

In the second quadrant (90° < θ < 180°), cosine is negative and sine is positive.

cos(120°) = -1/2 and sin(120°) = √3/2, so p = -1/2 + √3/2

As √3/2 > 1/2, the sum is greater than zero.

questions.question: If \(\rm secθ = \frac{65}{63}\) and θ is an acute angle, then the value of 8(cosecθ - cotθ) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm secθ = \frac{65}{63}\) and θ is an acute angle, then the value of 8(cosecθ - cotθ) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\rm secθ = \frac{65}{63}\) = Hypotenuse/Base

Formula used:

By Pythagoras theorem

H2 = P2 + B2

Calculation:

652 = P2 + 632

⇒ P = 16

8(cosecθ - cotθ) = 8(H/P - B/P)

⇒ 8(65/16 - 63/16) = 8 × 2/16 = 16/16

∴ The result = 1

questions.question: If sin x - 3cos x = \(\sqrt {3} \) cos x, then the value of cot x is ______.
questions.questionHtml: If sin x - 3cos x = \(\sqrt {3} \)cos x, then the value of cot x is ______.
questions.solution:
sin x – 3cos x =√3 cosx

On dividing both sides of the equation by cos x, we get

⇒ tan x – 3 = √3 ⇒ tan x = 3 + √3 ⇒ cot x = \(1 \over 3+√3\)

On rationalizing the numerator, we get

⇒ cot x =  \(1 \over 3+√3\)  × \(3 - √3 \over 3-√3\) ⇒ cot x = \(3- √3\over {3^2-3}\) = \(\frac{3-√3}{6}\)

questions.question: What is the value of \(\rm \left(\frac{1+\sec^2A}{1+\cos^2A}\right)\rm \left(\frac{1+\sin^2A}{1+cosec^2A}\right)\) ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of \(\rm \left(\frac{1+\sec^2A}{1+\cos^2A}\right)\rm \left(\frac{1+\sin^2A}{1+cosec^2A}\right)\)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume an angle, say A = 45°, to quickly evaluate the expression.

⇒ sec245° = 2, cos245° = 1/2, sin245° = 1/2, cosec245° = 2

⇒ Expression = [(1 + 2) ÷ (1 + 1/2)] × [(1 + 1/2) ÷ (1 + 2)]

⇒ Expression = (3 ÷ 3/2) × (3/2 ÷ 3) = 2 × 1/2 = 1

From the given options, tan245° = (1)2 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is tan2 A.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = [(1 + sec2A) ÷ (1 + cos2A)] × [(1 + sin2A) ÷ (1 + cosec2A)]

Formula Used:

sec A = 1 / cos A, cosec A = 1 / sin A, tan A = sin A / cos A

Calculations:

⇒ First part = (1 + 1/cos2A) ÷ (1 + cos2A)

⇒ First part = [(cos2A + 1) / cos2A] ÷ (1 + cos2A) = 1 / cos2A

⇒ Second part = (1 + sin2A) ÷ (1 + 1/sin2A)

⇒ Second part = (1 + sin2A) ÷ [(sin2A + 1) / sin2A] = sin2A

⇒ Complete Expression = (1 / cos2A) × sin2A

⇒ Expression = sin2A / cos2A = tan2A

∴ The correct answer is tan2 A.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

Functions that are inverted forms of each other: sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ and cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ.

Quotient Identities

These identities relate tan and cot to sine and cosine: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

Value Putting Technique

In the simplification of trigonometric expressions, substituting an angle like θ = 45° easily converts complex variables into numerals, aiding rapid elimination of wrong options.

questions.question: If 3sec 2 θ + tanθ - 7 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of \((\frac{2 sinθ +3 cosθ} {cosecθ +secθ})\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If 3sec2θ + tanθ - 7 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of  \((\frac{2 sinθ +3 cosθ} {cosecθ +secθ})\) ?
questions.solution:
3sec2θ + tanθ - 7 = 0

⇒ 3(1 + tan2θ) + tanθ - 7 = 0 ⇒ 3tan2θ + tanθ - 4 = 0 ⇒  3tan2θ + 4tanθ - 3tanθ - 4 = 0 ⇒ (tanθ - 1)(3tanθ + 4) = 0

Here, (tan θ - 1) = 0 ⇒ tan θ = 1 ⇒ θ = 45°   [(3tan θ + 4) = 0 ⇒ tan θ ≠ -\(4\over3\) ] 

\((\frac{2 sinθ +3 cosθ} {cosecθ +secθ})\) putting the value of θ, we get

⇒ \((\frac{2sin45 +3cos45} {cosec45 +sec45})\) ⇒ \({{2\times{1\over{\sqrt2}}}+{3\times{1\over{\sqrt2}}}}\over{\sqrt2+\sqrt2}\) ⇒ \({{2\over{\sqrt2}}+{3\over\sqrt2}}\over{2\sqrt2}\) ⇒ \({2+3}\over{\sqrt2\times{2\sqrt2}}\) ⇒ \(5\over4\)

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{sin23^\circ cos67^\circ tan45^\circ +cos23^\circ sin67^\circ cot45^\circ }{2sin45^\circ cos45^\circ }\) is:

sin(90° - θ) = cosθ

questions.question: The value of cosec (58° + θ) - sec (32° - θ) + sin 15° sin 35° sec 55° sin 30° sec 75° is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of cosec (58° + θ) - sec (32° - θ) + sin 15° sin 35° sec 55° sin 30° sec 75° is:

cosec (58° + θ) - sec (32° - θ) + sin 15° sin 35° sec 55° sin 30° sec 75°

Sin α × Cosec α = 1

Calculation:

⇒ sin 15° cosec 15° sin 35° cosec 35° sin 30°

⇒ 1/2

∴ The required value of cosec (58° + θ) - sec (32° - θ) + sin 15° sin 35° sec 55° sin 30° sec 75° is 1/2.

questions.question: If sinα + cosec α = tan \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) , then the value of (sin 3 α + cosec 3 α) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If sinα + cosec α = tan \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), then the value of (sin3α + cosec3α) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

sinα + cosec α = tan π/3

Formula used:

sin θ = 1/cosec θ 

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

Note: cosec θ represent cosec θ 

Calculation: 

sinα + cosec α = tan π/3

⇒ sinα + cosec α = √3       ------(1)

Now, taking cube both sides,

(sinα + cosec α)3 = (√3)3

By using identity (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ (sin3α + cosec3α) + 3 (sinα cosec α) (sinα + cosec α) = (√3)3

Since, sin α cosec α = 1 

⇒ (sin3α + cosec3α) + 3 × √3 = 3√3    [using equation (1)]

⇒ (sin3α + cosec3α) = 3√3 – 3√3

⇒ (sin3α + cosec3α) = 0

∴ The required value is 0
